newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian comittee wants court report on deputy PM.
newsitem.headline: Belgian comittee wants court report on deputy PM.

text.p: A Belgian parliamentary commission decided early on Thursday to recommend to parliament not to send deputy prime minister Elio Di Rupo before a court over allegations that he had had sex with minors.

Commission chairman Raymond Langendries told reporters that the 11-member commission, made up of representatives of the main political parties, instead wanted the highest court in the land to proceed with further investigations into the allegations and to submit a report by December 9 at the latest.
The commission made the recommendation after a marathon meeting which began on Wednesday afternoon and at which it discussed a dossier submitted to parliament by the Brussels public prosecutor.
Langendries said that a majority of the panel had voted in favour of a continuation of the investigation. It had heard the prosecutor and the minister in person.
"The prosecutor general's report was not complete enough to warrant lifting Di Rupo's immunity and refer him to court," commission member Renaat Landuyt told Reuters.
He added that as far as he was concerned Di Rupo did not have to step down. "It would be very unfortunate if Mr Di Rupo would have to resign at this stage," he said.
